newsitem.title: BELGIUM: NATO parliamentary body appoints new head.
newsitem.headline: NATO parliamentary body appoints new head.

text.p: NATO's parliamentary arm, the North Atlantic Assembly (NAA), has appointed Simon Lunn, a 55-year-old British man, as the organisation's new secretary- general, the NAA said in a statement on Thursday.

The NAA said Lunn -- a former aide of ex-NATO Secretary General Lord Carrington -- would take up his duties immediately. He replaces Peter Corterier, a former German minister, who retired last November.
"I am looking forward to leading the Secretariat during a period of fundamental reorientation for NATO," Lunn said.

The NAA, the forum in which members from the parliaments of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation's (NATO's) 16 countries meet and debate policy, is set to take on new roles after the alliance's planned enlargement and landmark pact with Russia.

"Enlargement, the new relationship with Russia and Ukraine, and an enhanced Partnership for Peace programme will all require active legislative involvement and a higher profile for the Assembly," Lunn added.
Lunn, married with two children, formerly held the position of NAA deputy secretary-general. From 1983-88, he was the head of the Plans and Policy Section at NATO's main Brussels headquarters.
